decision: Inclusion definition written and frozen before any screening, sha256 571df688fec8b25b3e0531d134118f39e2888ceba8e8e97cbbbe9636fb710332
Writing task in the conversation (not only the first turn) read as: the labeller reads every turn, and an included conversation needs a user turn after its first writing-task turn
why: Bet 1 judged only the first 3 user turns; a writing task with no later turn gives no follow-up to code
alternative_rejected: Requiring the task in turn 1, or in 2+ turns

decision: Contact patterns are masked, not dropped: 4,014 eligible records have an email or phone-like string in a user turn
why: Dropping them would remove personal statements and reports that carry a contact line; masked text stays in blind/ only

decision: Bet 1's 2,399 cached labels are not reused as labels. Its random 2,000 draw is reused as part of the random seed (281 eligible records), and old vs new labels are cross-tabbed there
why: Old labels used a research-only definition on the first 3 user turns, so no label maps cleanly to the new definition; the draw itself is random

decision: Screen labeller claude-sonnet-5-5 via claude -p, tools off, no session persistence, batches of about 90k characters, whole conversation with user turns cut to 1,500 and AI turns to 500 characters (caps shrink to fit 14k)
why: Same tool as Bet 1, cheap enough for thousands of conversations; caps keep long conversations readable
alternative_rejected: Subagents: harder to log per call

decision: Seed = 1,200 random eligible unused records, split train/test by hash; the test half is never used to fit
why: Random seed gives a prevalence estimate; a held-out half gives a rough recall

decision: Embedding model BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 rev 5c38ec7c405ec4b44b94cc5a9bb96e735b38267a (MIT), sentence-transformers 3.3.1, input = masked user turns, first 2,000 chars
why: Small open model, runs locally on all 139,736 records
alternative_rejected: Larger models: slower, no clear gain for ranking

decision: Audit labeller claude-opus-5-5 with its own prompt, fresh processes, accepted and rejected records shuffled together, never shown screen labels
why: Independence from the screen as far as available models allow; same vendor family is disclosed

decision: Accepted = screen INCLUDE with a user turn after the first writing turn; INCLUDE with first_writing_turn 0 read as turn 1
Coded sample drawn only from the random seed's accepted conversations (114), seeded order, one per IP cluster, until >=30 conversations and >=150 windows
why: Seed prevalence is 10%, so the random seed alone gives enough; drawing from the ranked pool would bring back keyword and embedding bias

decision: Long conversations: code turns 1 to 10 only, and the first writing turn must fall in that run. 3 of 35 conversations were capped, 20 later turns not coded
why: Keeps one conversation from dominating; turn 1 start keeps the whole-conversation reading
alternative_rejected: Coding a window around the writing turns

decision: Coder views: one part file per window (request, response, next user turn, uncut, contacts masked); coders read parts in order and label window NN before opening part NN+1
why: Gives full history up to the request without repeating it in every view; later turns are not in earlier parts
alternative_rejected: One whole-conversation file (shows the future); per-window files with repeated history (4x the reading)
